exposure: Computerized provider order entry (CPOE) for parenteral nutrition (PN)
outcome: Parenteral nutrition composition (energy, protein, lipid, carbohydrate intake)
cohort: A cohort of 94 extremely low-birth-weight (ELBW) preterm infants from a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit, born over a 1-year period, divided into two equal groups based on whether CPOE was used for PN.
finding: The introduction of CPOE for parenteral nutrition significantly increased the administration of energy, protein, lipid, and carbohydrates on days 1 and 7 of life, leading to lower initial weight loss, improved linear growth, and faster regain of birth weight in ELBW infants compared to manually calculated prescriptions.
